title: Singleton bound
statement:
Let $\alpha$ be a finite alphabet with at least two symbols, and let $C$ be a code of length $n$ over $\alpha$ — that is, a finite set of codewords $c : \mathrm{Fin}\,n \to \alpha$. Suppose $C$ has minimum distance $d$, meaning that some two distinct codewords of $C$ are at Hamming distance exactly $d$ and no two distinct codewords are at distance less than $d$. Then
\[
\abs{C} \;\le\; \abs{\alpha}^{\,n-d+1}.
\]
hypotheses_covered: alphabet is nontrivial (at least two symbols)
C is a code of length n over the alphabet
C has minimum distance d (distinct codewords realizing distance d, and no two distinct codewords closer than d)
replaced:
Assuming $\alpha$ is nontrivial, a code $C\subseteq\alpha^n$ with minimum distance $d$
satisfies
\[
|C| \;\le\; |\alpha|^{\,n-d+1}.
\]
